claims: A title plan supports the register and identifies the general extent of land in a registered title.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is recorded as determined under section 60.
Title plans can contain references to easements, covenants or land removed from the title.
The great majority of registered titles show general boundaries.
No standard tolerance, measurement or ratio maps a general-boundary line to the legal boundary.
Title-plan interpretation requires the register and underlying evidence; red edging must not be treated as survey precision.
A determined boundary records the exact line after that line has been identified; HMLR does not resolve the underlying dispute.
Determined-boundary plans identify start, end and turning points and require sufficient surrounding detail and a stated scale.
National Polygon publishes HMLR index polygons for England and Wales.
An index polygon is an index showing the indicative location of a registered title, not the legal boundary itself.
Title plan and register normally record the general position unless an exact determined boundary is recorded.

quality_guards: Do not promote an index polygon to an exact legal boundary.
Do not bind a candidate solely from red edging, polygon proximity or shared grid reference.
Require current title/register linkage and exact public polygon bytes before authoritative candidate binding.
Fail closed while current INSPIRE IDs and direct polygon bytes for the three candidates are absent.
